sections.heading: 1. Climb the ladder
lines: ① First days: walk comfortably, short steps.
② Double calf raises 15 × 3, within comfort.
③ Then single leg, add weight, small hops.
④ Drills and short games, comp last.

slides.title:
Get back on court

caption:
Felt a sharp grab in your calf mid-rally? Tennis and pickleball are full of quick push-offs and stop-start moves, and calf strains are common, especially late in a match or after a jump in how much you play.

Early on, keep walking comfortably and start gentle calf raises within comfort. Then progress to single-leg raises, add weight and small hops, and ease back in with drills and short games before competition. Most people return within a few weeks, depending on severity.

Get checked if you can't rise onto your toes, felt a kick to the back of the heel, or have calf swelling and warmth without a clear injury.
